questions.a: (a) Correct 90,09,009; 90,09,009 - 9,00,909 = 81,08,100 short. (b) 3,04,05,06,070: three arab four crore five lakh six thousand seventy. (c) The announcement names 5,70,03,800, which is 5,70,03,800 - 5,07,03,800 = 63,00,000 more than the real amount.

questions.q: A state bus corporation reported ticket revenue of ₹4,06,05,300 from city buses and ₹2,95,40,700 from rural buses. Its target for the year was seven crore rupees. (a) Write the city-bus revenue in words. (b) By how much does the city revenue exceed the rural revenue? Write the answer in figures. (c) Find the total revenue with Indian commas. (d) A refund of ₹1,50,000 to rural passengers has not yet been deducted, and the target is judged on revenue after refunds. Can the corporation announce that the target was met? Justify using your answers.
questions.a: (a) Four crore six lakh five thousand three hundred. (b) 4,06,05,300 - 2,95,40,700 = 1,10,64,600 (one crore ten lakh sixty four thousand six hundred). (c) 4,06,05,300 + 2,95,40,700 = 7,01,46,000. (d) No. After the refund the revenue is 7,01,46,000 - 1,50,000 = 6,99,96,000, which is ₹4,000 short of 7,00,00,000, although the unadjusted total (c) was above the target.
s: Part (a): names the city revenue as four crore six lakh five thousand three hundred
Part (b): subtracts to 1,10,64,600
Part (c): adds to 7,01,46,000
Part (d): subtracts the refund to get 6,99,96,000 and says the target is missed by 4,000

questions.q: A clerk was told to enter 'sixty lakh seven thousand eighty five' but keyed 6,07,085. (a) Write the amount he should have keyed in figures and say what his entry actually reads as in words. (b) By how much is the entry short of the real amount?
questions.a: (a) Correct: 60,07,085. His 6,07,085 reads 'six lakh seven thousand eighty five': the 6 sits in the lakh place instead of the ten-lakh place. (b) 60,07,085 - 6,07,085 = 54,00,000 (fifty four lakh).
s: Part (a): writes 60,07,085 and reads the entry as six lakh seven thousand eighty five
Part (b): finds the shortfall 54,00,000

Part (b): spots 70 thousand read as 7 thousand and writes 50,07,030

questions.q: The annual day of Saraswati Vidyalaya, Pune, raised money for a new library. Ticket sales brought in ₹18,40,250, the food stalls ₹7,06,300 and donations ₹2,03,075. The library needs ₹27,50,000. The notice board committee must decide what the headline may say. (a) Find the total collection in rupees, using Indian commas. (b) By how much does the total exceed 27 lakh? Write that amount in words. (c) How much is still needed to reach ₹27,50,000? (d) A late donor now gives ₹500. May the headline say 'More than ₹27,50,000 collected'? Give a reason using your answer to (c).
questions.a: (a) 18,40,250 + 7,06,300 + 2,03,075 = ₹27,49,625. (b) 27,49,625 - 27,00,000 = 49,625: forty nine thousand six hundred twenty five. (c) 27,50,000 - 27,49,625 = ₹375. (d) Yes. The donor's ₹500 is more than the ₹375 still needed, so the total becomes 27,50,125, which is more than 27,50,000.
s: Part (a): adds the three amounts to get 27,49,625 with Indian commas
Part (b): finds 49,625 above 27 lakh and names it in words
Part (c): finds the shortfall 375 to 27,50,000
Part (d): says yes because 500 is more than the 375 needed (total 27,50,125)

questions.q: Arjun writes 'ten lakh twenty thousand' as 10,020,000 because 'a comma always comes after every three digits'. Is he right? Explain, and write the correct figure.
questions.a: No. 10,020,000 groups the digits in threes (American style) and is 1,00,20,000 in the Indian system, i.e. one crore twenty thousand, nearly ten times as big as the intended number. Ten lakh twenty thousand is 10,20,000: the first comma after three digits from the right, then one after every two digits.
s: Gives the verdict that Arjun is wrong
Shows his figure equals one crore twenty thousand (3-3 grouping gives a different, much larger number)
Writes 10,20,000 and states the 3-2-2 comma rule

questions.q: A clerk copies the number 6,57,03,210 but drops its last 0 and re-inserts commas, writing 65,70,321. (a) How many times as large as his copy is the real number? (b) State the value of the digit 7 in the real number and the value of the digit 7 in his copy.
questions.a: (a) 6,57,03,210 = 65,70,321 x 10, so the real number is 10 times his copy. (b) In the real number the 7 is in the lakh place, worth 7,00,000. In the copy it is in the ten-thousands place, worth 70,000.
s: Part (a): sees dropping the last zero makes the copy one tenth, so the real number is 10 times as large
Part (b): gives 7,00,000 for the real number and 70,000 for the copy

Part (b): 10 five-digit and 15 six-digit tokens

s: Writes the figure 7,12,00,000
Notes the largest 7-digit number is 99,99,999, below one crore
Concludes a number of crores needs 8 digits so 7 digits is impossible

questions.q: Four towns have populations P = 48,05,000, Q = 4,80,500, R = 48,50,000 and S = 4,85,000. (a) Arrange them in increasing order and state the rule you used to compare. (b) Find the difference between the largest and the smallest population and write it in words. (c) Which pairs of towns together have fewer than 50 lakh people?
questions.a: (a) Q < S < P < R (4,80,500 < 4,85,000 < 48,05,000 < 48,50,000). Q and S have 6 digits so they are smaller than the 7-digit P and R; among numbers with the same number of digits compare from the left. (b) 48,50,000 - 4,80,500 = 43,69,500: forty three lakh sixty nine thousand five hundred. (c) Only Q and S: 4,80,500 + 4,85,000 = 9,65,500. Any pair with P or R has more than 50 lakh (the smallest such pair, P + Q, is 52,85,500).
s: Part (a): orders Q, S, P, R
Part (a): states the digit count then left-to-right rule
Part (b): finds 43,69,500
Part (b): names it in words
Part (c): picks only Q and S, checking that every pair with P or R exceeds 50 lakh

questions.q: A Chennai cricket academy received two sponsorships: ₹15,00,00,000 from an Indian firm and 120 million rupees from a firm in the USA. Part (b): 15 + 12 = 27 crore

Links 100 crore to one arab = one billion

questions.q: A school's old coupon counter has only +100 and +1000 buttons. The treasurer wants it to show ₹47,300. (a) Write an expression for 47,300 with the fewest clicks on this counter and count the clicks. (b) Can the counter show ₹47,350? Explain. (c) The school adds a +10000 button. Part (b): says no because only multiples of 100 can be shown

s: Part (b): says every number shown is a multiple of 100

Does he reach 4,06,308, and how many clicks did he use? (c) Which single button can replace Rohit's 40 presses of +10000, and how many clicks does that save? (d) Rohit says he can do it in 20 clicks. (c) 40 x 10,000 = 4 x 1,00,000, so +100000 pressed 4 times replaces 40 presses and saves 36 clicks (57 - 36 = 21). s: Part (a): fewest clicks 21 from the digits 4,0,6,3,0,8
Part (b): confirms 4,06,308 and counts 57 clicks
Part (c): replaces 40 presses of +10000 by 4 of +100000, saving 36 clicks
Part (d): says 20 is impossible because the replaced method reaches the minimum 21

Shows every multiple of 1,000 is a multiple of 100, so the first half holds
Gives a counterexample such as 70 for the second half

questions.q: (a) Give a 9-digit number in which exchanging any two digits always gives a bigger number. (b) How many such 9-digit numbers are there? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 123456789. (b) Only one. Exchanging two digits makes the number bigger only if the smaller digit is on the left, so the digits must be in strictly increasing order from the left (equal digits would give the same number). A 0 cannot start the number and cannot come later in an increasing order, so the nine digits are 1 to 9, giving just 123456789.
s: Part (b): exactly one, because the digits must be strictly increasing and 0 cannot be used

Part (b): says no because only multiples of 100 can be shown
